newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Russia leads foreign investment to ex-Soviet world.
newsitem.headline: Russia leads foreign investment to ex-Soviet world.

text.p: Russia has led foreign direct investments to the ex-Soviet Union with $6.6 billion as of 1996 while Moldova and Belarus were at the bottom of the league with just $104 million and $350 million, respectively, a report said.

The U.N. Economic Commission for Europe (ECE), a specialised United Nations agency for economic cooperation in Europe, said in a report on Tuesday Kazakhstan ranked second in foreign direct investments to the ex-Soviet world with $3.24 billion.
Ukraine came third with $1.1 billion, followed by Estonia with $680 million, said the report, based on official data from central banks as of mid-1996.

Western Europe accounted for the bulk of foreign direct investment, with an 80 percent share in Belarus, 70 percent in Russia and 60 percent in Estonia, Ukraine and Latvia but only 17 percent in Kazakhstan.
